title: Field-Free Transverse Aharonov--Bohm Phase Gate for an Orbital $l$-Qubit
abstract: Free-space Aharonov--Bohm (AB) Bessel modes are known to carry a flux-dependent azimuthal Schrödinger probability current and kinetic orbital angular momentum. We extend this response to the spin-resolved conserved Dirac current of a core-excluded finite-wall annular guide and show that confinement converts its surviving orbital component into a transverse Aharonov--Bohm (TAB) propagation phase for a straight traveling mode whose centroid path has zero projection onto $\mathbf A$. The radial-gradient current reverses under spin reversal; retaining the complete evanescent tail closes it as a boundary contribution, leaving a spin-independent orbital phase $Δφ_{ln}\propto lΦL_{\rm int}\langleρ^{-2}\rangle_{ln}/v_z$. Opposite-winding modes $|\pm l\rangle$ form a same-path qubit implementing $R_z(2δ_l)$ with differential readout and common-mode phase rejection, while direct first-order crosstalk requires the angular harmonic $m=\pm2l$. For a $100\,μ\mathrm{m}$ section with $a=20\,\mathrm{nm}$, $R=30\,\mathrm{nm}$, $E_z=10\,\mathrm{meV}$, and $|l|=10$, the sensitivity is $0.1885\,\mathrm{mrad/mG}$ and $R_z(π)$ occurs at $16.67\,\mathrm{G}$. Finite-wall confinement thus turns intrinsic azimuthal Dirac current into a guided field-free phase operation.
summary: The paper proposes using the Aharonov-Bohm effect in a confined annular waveguide to create a field-free transverse phase gate for an orbital $l$-qubit. By analyzing the spin-resolved Dirac current, they show that confinement stabilizes a measurable relative phase $\Delta\phi_{TAB}$ proportional to the magnetic flux and angular momentum quantum number. This offers a pathway toward robust quantum information processing using engineered electromagnetic potentials.
main_problem: To demonstrate a field-free transverse Aharonov–Bohm (TAB) phase gate for an orbital $l$-qubit.
main_result: Confinement in a finite-wall annular guide converts the intrinsic azimuthal Dirac current into a guided, reproducible phase operation $\Delta\phi_{TAB}$, enabling robust qubit manipulation.
method: The phase is calculated by analyzing the spin-resolved conserved Dirac current and comparing two equivalent methods: integrating the transverse current texture or calculating the flux-induced angular-energy expectation value shift.
model_or_system: The system models an electron wave propagating in a core-excluded finite-wall annular guide, supporting spin-resolved Dirac modes $|\pm langle$ which form the qubit basis.
key_observables: The measurable quantity is the normalized differential contrast $C_\chi$, which directly yields the relative phase $2\delta_l$.
important_parameters: Key parameters include the angular momentum quantum number $|l|$, the magnetic flux $\Phi$, and geometric dimensions like inner radius $a$ and outer radius $R$.
main_assumptions: The analysis is performed to leading nonrelativistic order, assuming a straight annular guide geometry with core exclusion.
figures_summary: Figure 1 illustrates the physical setup showing flux outside the electron wave support. Figure 2 details the full gate operation: balanced input $	o$ TAB section ($R_z(2\delta_l)$) $	o$ analyzer ($\chi$) $	o$ output contrast $C_\chi$.
paper_structure: The paper develops the theory by extending free-space AB effects to confined Dirac modes, deriving the phase shift $\Delta E_{ln}(\Phi)$, showing how opposite winding modes form a qubit basis $\{|+langle, |-langle\}$, and finally detailing the interferometric readout scheme using differential contrast $C_\chi$.
why_interesting: This work provides a concrete theoretical blueprint for realizing quantum gates using fundamental electromagnetic interactions (AB effect) within solid-state or nanoscale structures, which is highly relevant to superconducting circuits and semiconductor quantum computing.
